ranked.headline: Validated computational inference links chromatin and transcription to gene regulation
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics methods now pair gene-level regulatory inference with explicit validation and technical-variation handling.

ranked.headline: Genetic and epigenetic variation jointly reshape gene regulation in disease tissues
ranked.summary: Cell-type-resolved eQTL, methylation and chromatin maps now test variant prioritization against external clinical and GWAS anchors.

ranked.headline: Histology and spatial transcriptomics are being fused via multimodal learning models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and journal papers pair histology, imaging and spatial expression data through foundation models, contrastive learning and 3D reconstruction.

ranked.headline: AI models condition molecular design on explicit binding, response, and pathway criteria
ranked.summary: Recent work couples generation and perturbation selection to structure-aware, QSAR, and mechanistic predictors within a single iterative loop.

ranked.headline: Graph and generative models score peptide, epitope and binder candidates from structure
ranked.summary: Structure-aware and generative models now predict epitope recognition and design peptides directly from predicted complex structures.

ranked.headline: Learned models fuse heterogeneous evidence to predict function; benchmarks expose limits
ranked.summary: Benchmarks across genomic, single-cell, and LLM-based tasks now test whether learned predictions generalize beyond their training settings.

ranked.headline: Geometric and temporal representations of single-cell and imaging omics data
ranked.summary: Single-cell benchmarks and atlases now test whether temporal, topological, or information-geometric structure improves representations of cell states.

ranked.headline: Learned models now score protein interfaces, ligands, and complex structures
ranked.summary: Cryo-EM density maps and language model embeddings now feed predictors of interface, ligand, and binding affinity outputs.

ranked.headline: Deep sequence models decode TF binding, promoter logic, and gene expression regulation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers extend sequence-to-regulation models with spacing-aware, foundation-model, and changepoint-based approaches.

ranked.headline: Faster, leaner algorithms and pipelines for sequence and structure analysis
ranked.summary: Large-scale protein, RNA and genome analyses in these items target runtime, memory and throughput bottlenecks.

ranked.headline: Open-source Snakemake and R/Python tools automate genomic and epigenomic analyses
ranked.summary: Recent journal and preprint releases push reproducible, modular pipelines and packages into cancer, methylation, and regulatory genomics.

ranked.headline: Structure-informed methods refine viral taxonomy and protein family assignment
ranked.summary: Structural evidence is being combined with profile-based methods to resolve divergent viral lineages where sequence similarity alone is limited.

ranked.headline: Tree-structured models recover ancestral history and lineage from phylogenetic data
ranked.summary: Three recent items pair explicit probabilistic or combinatorial machinery with formal guarantees on tree recovery.

ranked.headline: mtDNA copy number decouples from expression while CpG mutation rates track methylation
ranked.summary: New preprints and a 2026 publication sharpen separation of mtDNA copy number from expression and of methylation effects on CpG mutation rates.

ranked.headline: Deep generative and transformer models infer regulatory networks from single-cell data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair scRNA with scATAC priors and GRN graph models, moving regulatory inference toward interpretable, prior-informed frameworks.

ranked.headline: Language models and co-folding tools tested for design, stability and ligand pose
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple protein language and co-folding models with external tools, fine-tuning or benchmarks for design, stability and binding tasks.

ranked.headline: Systematic bias and reproducibility failures in biological ML and statistical inference
ranked.summary: Recent studies show biological ML and statistical models yield biased or inflated performance, prompting new correction and reproducibility frameworks.

ranked.headline: Structure-based motif search and paralog inference extend functional annotation
ranked.summary: Folddisco and CB-Search publish motif search methods, while a preprint pairs Foldseek with family-specific regression to nominate paralogs.

ranked.headline: Simulations resolve binding routes and contact networks in diverse drug targets
ranked.summary: MD, QM/MM and ML-guided enhanced sampling now resolve binding pathways for enzyme, disordered-protein and designed-peptide targets.

ranked.headline: Inferring cell and tissue states from routine molecular profiles
ranked.summary: Routine bulk transcriptomic and multi-omic data are being evaluated against alternative pipelines and benchmarks for biomarker inference.

ranked.headline: AI and statistical tools generate divergent protein conformational ensembles
ranked.summary: Predictors yield distinct conformational distributions and miss bound-state disorder, so ensemble outputs require cautious validation before interpretation.

ranked.headline: Enhancer-promoter contacts and RBP logic resolve regulatory control of gene expression
ranked.summary: Multi-omic single-cell atlases and interpretable models now enable mechanistic dissection of regulatory control across cell types and conditions.

ranked.headline: Omics foundation models gain ancestry-aware evaluation and generative adaptation
ranked.summary: Disparity-focused benchmarks and tabular foundation models now test whether omics representations generalize equitably across ancestry groups.

ranked.headline: Reproducible workflows for bacterial strain, genome and resistance sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Recent tools bundle long-read assembly, strain genotyping and AMR prediction into automated, reproducible microbial analysis workflows.

ranked.headline: Refining uncertain biological models via perturbation design and Bayesian inference
ranked.summary: Mechanistic signaling and regulatory models are being constrained by perturbation design, bootstrapped connectivity inference, and Bayesian priors.

ranked.headline: Structure-aware sparse models for genomic interaction and expression analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications build LD, TSS, hierarchy, and multi-omic structure directly into statistical models of high-dimensional genomic data.

ranked.headline: Models map tau spread, gene expression and genetic risk in Alzheimer's disease
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply attribution, generative and survival models to individual-level AD readouts across imaging, connectomics and genomics.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-level methods refine introgression and selection inference in genomic data
ranked.summary: Recent updates to S*, HMM, and pooled-sequencing selection methods target archaic introgression and polygenic adaptation under linkage disequilibrium.

ranked.headline: Gene duplication and transposable elements shape genome evolution across eukaryotes
ranked.summary: Chromosome-scale assemblies from water lily, ant, and cricket now sit alongside comparative analyses of duplication and TE dynamics.

ranked.headline: Graph neural networks encode molecular and spatial relationships for omics analysis
ranked.summary: Recent bioinformatics and preprint work applies graph learning to spatial transcriptomics and multi-omics data for domain, niche, and feature discovery.

ranked.headline: Reference choice and error modeling govern somatic variant and fusion detection accuracy
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that reference structure and background error models shape sensitivity in low-frequency somatic and cfDNA variant detection.

ranked.headline: Computational restoration of usable structure from noisy electron microscopy data
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 publications extend sparse, prompt-based, and registration-guided methods to cryo-ET, cryo-EM picking, and serial-section EM.

ranked.headline: New open-source tools for genome annotation, alignment visualisation and molecular maps
ranked.summary: Recent software papers add reusable, programmatically accessible tools for specific genomic and molecular data workflow steps.

ranked.headline: Coarse-grained and machine-learning models of protein dynamics, disorder, and host binding
ranked.summary: Physics-based simulation is now paired with machine learning to infer potentials, design disordered proteins, and map viral glycoprotein interactions.

ranked.headline: Computational tools decode cell communication, protein function and oxidized lipids
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair learned models and mass spectrometry workflows to prioritize cell, protein, immune, and lipid features for follow-up.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools and resources for reproducible omics analysis and visualization
ranked.summary: Scalable, reproducible software for large omics datasets is appearing alongside curated resources for aging genes and lipidomics workflows.

ranked.headline: Non-model reference genomes now paired with evolutionary and functional interpretation
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 reports pair reference-grade genomes and proteomes with evolutionary and functional analyses across eukaryotes.

ranked.headline: Bacterial genomics spans AMR forecasting, nanopore detection and strain nomenclature
ranked.summary: Genome-based AMR forecasting to 2050 and real-time nanopore panel visualisation extend bacterial genomic data toward rapid pathogen detection and surveillance.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools automate microscopy image segmentation and quantification
ranked.summary: Recent bioRxiv and PubMed releases present accessible GUI and Python tools for segmenting and quantifying microscopy images.

ranked.headline: Long-read isoform models are coupled to proteomic evidence for protein-level discovery
ranked.summary: Long-read transcript models and top-down mass spectrometry are now being matched to peptide and proteoform evidence.
